newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht nervous late after finmin appointment.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht nervous late after finmin appointment.

text.p: The Thai baht was still cautious against the dolalr in the domestic and offshore markets despite the appointment of new finance minister Thanong Bidaya on Friday, dealers said.

"The strong buying of the dollar eased a bit from yestereday," said one senior dealer at a local bank. "I don't think they were impressed with the appointment. It's still cautious and they just wait and see."
The baht was quoted at 26.000/26.100 to the dollar late in the domestic market compared with 25.900/26.000 in the morning.
The Bank of Thailand set the mid-rate at 25.79.

Dealers said the market remained concern about economic policy continuity following Thanong's appointment. The incoming new minister is known as a low profile banker with less credentials than predecessor Amnuay Viravan.
"He is little known among the prospective candidates. We are also concerned about policy continuity," said another dealer at a foreign bank.
In the offshore market, the baht firmed to 25.000/25.300 to the dollar near the close after falling to as low as 26.000 in the afternoon and against 25.300/25.600 in the early morning.
"The (baht) sentiment remained weak. But people are reluctant to short baht on high (baht) short-term borrowings," said one Singapore-based dealer.
The one-month swap premium was traded at 22/32 satangs per dollar in the domestic market and 200/220 satang offshore.
The overnight interbank rate was quoted at 16.00-18.00 percent in late trade compared with 19.00 in the morning.
